adversarial.assessment: All 19 checks behave per the spec's Errors table. Observations, none a defect: (1) a trailing newline in changed_paths counts the push (the empty last segment is not under .legion/) -- conservative, and the listener never emits one; (2) '.legion/../src/a.ts' is prefix-classified handoff-only -- GitHub paths are normalized and never contain '..'; (3) two handoff-only pushes A then B both delivered before either synchronize leave the round counted once (A counted, B consumed) -- exactly the spec's 'several pushes ... the round counts at most once' row, truth would be 0.

observations: PR body 'Deploy skew' paragraph and .legion/implement.json deploySkewNote still say PR #966 'sits at fixAttempts=6' and will publish pr-blocked once more after the upgrade; #966 merged 2026-09-12T18:22Z and is a tombstone in live state, so that sentence is stale (no committed doc repeats it). Wording only.

Workspace hygiene: OMP writes an empty .omp/config.yml into the issue workspace at session start (every legion-* workspace has one; it is not gitignored). The implementer left @ on its handoff commit 2c808fbd, so my session's first `jj status` snapshot amended that commit into a divergent local copy e5cf55e3 (change kulvkspq). I moved my working copy with `jj new 2c808fbd`; the pushed head is untouched and my handoff is a child of 2c808fbd. The divergent e5cf55e3 is left in place (never abandoned per the worker skill) for the architect to abandon. Ending a phase with `jj new` (empty @) avoids this; adding .omp/ to .gitignore would remove the cause.

The daemon restarted repeatedly during this phase (04:07, 04:11, down again ~04:20 and ~04:22 UTC); in the gaps the bash tool could not mint LEGION_GRANT ('Unable to connect'), and, as the implementer also saw, a call with two injected LEGION_GRANT exports 403s on the second value.
